results.translation: 54. Of the kingdom, Tyndis is a coastal village of Keprobotros, notable; and Muziri is of the same kingdom, flourishing by the ships coming to it from Ariake and by the Greek ones; and it lies beside a river, being distant from Tyndis through the river and through the sea five hundred stadia, and from the one at it twenty. And Nelkynda is distant from Muziri about five hundred stadia, similarly through a river and on foot and through the sea, and it is of another kingdom, that of Pandion; and it too lies beside a river, as it were about one hundred twenty stadia from the sea.

results.translation: 56. Large ships sail to these trading posts because of the bulk and quantity of pepper and malabathrum. A great deal of money is sent ahead to it, chrysolite, simple clothing not much, multicolored fabrics, stibium, coral, raw glass, copper, tin, lead, wine not much, about as much as in Barygaza, realgar, arsenic, and grain as much as will suffice for those concerned with the ship's operation, because the merchants do not use it. Pepper is brought, being produced uniquely in one place of these trading posts, in the so-called Kottonarike, a considerable and varied amount; and pearl is also brought, and ivory, and Seric linen, and spikenard, the Gangetic kind, and malabathrum from the interior regions to it, and transparent stones of all kinds, and diamond, and hyacinth, and tortoise shell both the Chrysonesian kind and that hunted around the islands lying off Limyrike itself. Those who set out from Egypt in season sail to it around the month of July, which is Epiphi.
results.back_translation: 56. Μεγάλα πλοῖα πλέουσιν εἰς τὰ ἐμπόρια ταῦτα διὰ τὸ μέγεθος καὶ τὸ πλῆθος τοῦ πεπέρεως καὶ τοῦ μαλαβάθρου. Χρήματα πολλὰ προπέμπεται εἰς αὐτά, χρυσόλιθος, ἱμάτια ἁπλᾶ οὐ πολλά, ἱμάτια ποικίλα, στίβιον, κοράλλιον, ὕαλος ὠμή, χαλκός, κασσίτερος, μόλυβδος, οἶνος οὐ πολύς, ὅσον περ ἐν Βαρυγάζῃ, ῥεαλγάρ, ἀρσενικόν, καὶ σῖτος ὅσος ἂν ἱκανὸς ᾖ τοῖς περὶ τὴν τοῦ πλοίου ἐργασίαν, ὅτι οἱ ἔμποροι αὐτῷ οὐ χρῶνται. Πέπερι φέρεται, γεννώμενον μόνον ἐν ἑνὶ τόπῳ τῶν ἐμπορίων τούτων, ἐν τῇ λεγομένῃ Κοττοναρικῇ, πλῆθος ἱκανὸν καὶ ποικίλον· καὶ μαργαρῖται φέρονται, καὶ ἐλέφας, καὶ λίνον Σηρικόν, καὶ νάρδος, ἡ Γαγγητικὴ εἶδος, καὶ μαλάβαθρον ἐκ τῶν ἐσωτέρω χωρῶν εἰς αὐτά, καὶ λίθοι διαφανεῖς πάντων εἰδῶν, καὶ ἀδάμας, καὶ ὑάκινθος, καὶ χελώνης ὄστρακον ἥ τε ἡ Χρυσονησιακὴ εἶδος καὶ ἡ θηρευομένη περὶ τὰ νησία τὰ κείμενα ἀπὸ τῆς Λιμυρικῆς αὐτῆς. Οἱ ἐξαποστέλλοντες ἀπὸ Αἰγύπτου κατὰ καιρὸν πλέουσιν εἰς αὐτὴν περὶ τὸν μῆνα Ἰούλιον, ὅς ἐστιν Ἐπιφί.

That long-waisted woman, well indeed,
Even if rare deeds and precious things are obtained easily,
I shall not go—Hail, O my heart!—the Cheras
Where the foam of the Periyar river of Sulliyan churns,
The excellent vessel given by the Yavanas,
Coming with gold and departing with meat,
The prosperous Musiri rises with abundance,
Having crossed the difficult strait, the ford is worn,
The long noble elephant, the warrior of fierce battle, the fertile one,
In the fort where the banner sways, the gathering fortress,
Many-wheeled chariots, victorious banners raised high,
In the unfailing festival, on the tall mountain,
Extended by the bees, in the blue waters of the deep pool,
Like the doe with flowers facing it, this woman
In the rain-eyed gaze of the lion-rutting one, receives the cool dew.

results.translation: 4. After Ptolemais of the Beasts, at a distance of about three thousand stadia, there is a lawful trading post, Adulis, situated in a deep gulf facing directly south, in front of which lies an island called Oreine, distant from the innermost gulf about two hundred stadia toward the open sea, and having the mainland adjacent on both sides, where the ships that are brought down now anchor because of the raids from the land. And on the very mainland in Oreine, at a distance of twenty stadia from the sea, is Adulis, a moderate-sized village, from which to Koloe, an inland city and the first trading post for elephant, is a journey of three days. From this place to the very metropolis of the so-called Auxomites is another five days, to which all the elephant is brought from beyond the Nile through the so-called Kyenaion, and from there to Adulis.
